note: Inputs only: endpoint table (120 min). The K2SO4 row is the endpoint of the run plotted as Diag 5.8 (see data/digitized_inputs/polatides2007thesis_diag5p8_xcheck).

files.extracted.csv: tidy long: one row per electrolyte x quantity

csv_columns.table_row: row order in the printed table

csv_columns.pH_initial: pH column of the table (initial pH)

provenance.citation: Polatides C., Electrochemical removal of nitrate from aqueous solutions and environmental samples using constant and pulsed potential, PhD thesis (in Greek), Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Dept. of Chemical Engineering (2007); supervisor G. Kyriacou
provenance.caption_translated: Table 5.14. Degree of nitrate removal (%RE) and product selectivities (%S) in various supporting electrolytes. Electrolysis duration 120 min, at potential -2.0 V. Columns: supporting electrolyte | pH | %RE NO3- | %S NO2- | %S NH3 | %S N2.
provenance.source_file: page text layer from the archive's online reader (scratch only, not committed)

conditions.pH_change_unbuffered: K2SO4 run: initial pH 7, final pH 10.3 after 120 min at -2.0 V (printed p. 108)
conditions.cell: divided Teflon cell, Nafion 117 (ch. 4); 20 mL catholyte
conditions.gas_analysis: N2 by on-line GC-TCD, instantaneous concentration integrated over the He flow (ch. 4)

text_translated: Printed p. 108: 'the differences in the rate of nitrate reduction and in the selectivity of the products when buffers of pH 7 and pH 9.4 were used, relative to the unbuffered 0.1 M K2SO4, lie within the experimental error'; the rate is independent of pH in the range 7-9, in agreement with anion-reduction theory (pH dependence only for pH 0-4).

checks.cross_check_diag5p8: data/digitized_inputs/polatides2007thesis_diag5p8_xcheck reads the 120 min points of the K2SO4 run as RE 97.8 %, NO2 17.1 %, NH3 40.6 %, N2 32.7 % (N2 x 2), against 98.1/17.5/41.0/33.6 here.
checks.nh3_to_n2_ratio_text_p96: Printed p. 96 gives an NH3:N2 selectivity ratio of 2.44 for 120 min electrolysis of 0.1 M K2SO4 + 0.05 M KNO3 at -2.0 V. From this table 41.0/33.6 = 1.22 on the N-atom basis; 41.0/(33.6/2) = 2.44 only if N2 is counted per molecule.

transcription_method: thesis text layer: per-page text layer of the National Archive of PhD Theses online reader (EKT freader), read and typed in by an agent on 2026-10-20; table layout reconstructed by hand from the flattened text; every row's printed number sequence was checked by script to occur verbatim on the cited page (literature/extraction_scripts/thesis_tables/build_tables.py). Page images of these pages were not viewed. Not yet re-checked by a person.
